analyst.summary: Jindal Steel has genuinely completed a large capacity expansion — its Angul plant doubled to 12 million tonnes a year in March 2026, taking total capacity to 15.6 million tonnes — and management is guiding 21-27% volume growth for FY27 off capacity that already exists. That part is real. But profit per tonne of steel actually fell last year even as volumes hit a record, because raw-material costs rose faster than steel prices recovered, and the stock trades at roughly 31 times last year's earnings against a return on equity of only about 7-8%. The balance sheet is in better shape — credit rating just upgraded, debt levels improving — and government import duties support domestic steel prices. But the share price already assumes the expanded capacity will ramp up smoothly and margins will recover meaningfully — two things that have not happened together yet, and this company's own history shows expansions taking years longer than first announced. We rate it Sell on valuation grounds, not on the underlying growth story.
